title: An equivalence of sites preserving and reflecting coverings and its quasi-inverse define morphisms of sites
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal C$ be sites in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Let $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ be an equivalence of categories such that a family $\{X_a\to X\}_{a\in I}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal A$ with common target is a covering of $\mathcal A$ if and only if $\{p(X_a)\to p(X)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. Let $p':\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ be a quasi-inverse, with natural isomorphisms $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\cong p'\circ p$ and $\varepsilon:p\circ p'\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. Then: (1) a family $\{Y_a\to Y\}_{a\in I}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$ if and only if $\{p'(Y_a)\to p'(Y)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal A$; (2) $p$ and $p'$ are continuous (Sites, Definition 00WV, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)); (3) the functors $p^s:\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ p$ from sheaves of sets (resp. abelian sheaves) on $\mathcal C$ to those on $\mathcal A$ and $p'^s:\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F\circ p'$ in the other direction are quasi-inverse equivalences of categories; (4) $p_s$ and $p'_s$ on sheaves of sets are exact, so $p$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ and $p'$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ (Sites, Definition 00X1), and $p_s$ is a quasi-inverse of $p^s$, $p'_s$ a quasi-inverse of $p'^s$.

proof.text: Write a presieve as ofArrows. Transport coverings in both directions along epsilon using site_covering_isomorphic_family; naturality gives each commuting square. Apply hcover to R.map p' to obtain covering symmetry.
Equivalence.mk p p' eta epsilon makes p' an equivalence. Equivalences preserve limits, hence both functors preserve every cospan limit, including the required covering pullbacks.

Apply siteContinuous_pushforward_isSheaf separately to p and p', with the forward and reverse covering implications and the preceding pullback preservation. Convert the Type-valued sheaf predicate to construct both IsContinuous witnesses.

Mathlib sheafPushforwardContinuousComp followed by sheafPushforwardContinuousId' for epsilon and eta.symm constructs the two inverse-composition isomorphisms, uniformly for Type u and AddCommGrpCat. These give equivalence instances for both set-valued pushforwards.

Use Functor.sheafAdjunctionContinuous for each functor. An adjunction with equivalence right adjoint has equivalence left adjoint (Adjunction.isEquivalence_left_of_isEquivalence_right). Its unit and counit are isomorphisms, giving the four pullback/pushforward inverse-composition isomorphisms. Its toEquivalence.symm.toAdjunction makes the pullback a right adjoint, giving preservation of limits and then finite limits; as a left adjoint it preserves colimits and finite colimits. Assemble all clauses as a conjunction and two existential witnesses.
